texts: good. parses as a 43-member Keeper group with a fireable rule handing 'active' to each member, and 'in the present generation' is carried on that group, so nothing is dropped.
good. Pell is typed as a Keeper with 'young' kept as a separate description rather than fused into the role.

bad: the parse invents a ranking — it records Pell as holding second place in some year-ordering, which the sentence never states — and 'second-year' has no licensed internal analysis, so the tenure survives only as an opaque label. Say the tenure in its own clause instead: "Pell is a Keeper. He has been a Keeper for two years." — substitute whatever elapsed time 'second-year' means for you; a stated duration is what parses cleanly.
good. both halves land: 'Old Vesh' stays one whole name and the predicate 'old' becomes a separate property of him, with the Keeper typing intact.

mixed: the retirement itself is fine (a past retiring with Old Vesh as the retiree), but 'station-tending' forces the translator to coin a compound activity symbol whose internal object atom has no licensed home outside modal terms, and whether 'from' names a source or a plain preposition is unsettled — so the activity he retired from may not match downstream queries. Make the activity a finite clause: "Old Vesh has retired, and he no longer tends a station."

bad: the name got split — the parse records him as 'Vesh' and turns the 'Old' of his name into a separate claim that he is old — and the bare 'Council' falls between the translator's rule for a named institution and its rule for a definite one. Write "Old Vesh attends the Council." so the institution gets ordinary definite handling; if the name still splits, "The Council is attended by Old Vesh." also moves the name off the sentence-initial slot, where a capitalized epithet cannot be told apart from an ordinary adjective.

good. the teaching, Old Vesh as the teacher and the apprentices as the ones taught all come through; the adjudicator confirmed the role given to 'apprentices' is correct, so the earlier flag is not a defect.
